label: Pipeline Architecture & Reliability Fundamentals
desc: 11 interview questions covering Batch Design, Streaming, Reliability, Data Quality and more.

subs.label: Batch Design
subs.desc: How would you design a batch analytics pipeline?

subs.label: Streaming
subs.desc: How would you design a near-real-time ingestion pipeline?

subs.label: Reliability
subs.desc: How do you ensure idempotency in data pipelines? What reliability patterns do you use for production data pipelines?

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: How do you handle late-arriving events and backfills?

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: Streaming is chosen for low latency and continuous updates, but it adds real complexity — state management, ordering, exactly-once semantics.

subs.label: Data Modeling
subs.desc: What is the raw/silver/gold layering pattern, and why use it?

subs.label: Platform Design
subs.desc: How do you design a multi-tenant data platform?

subs.label: Schema
subs.desc: How do you handle schema evolution in a data platform?

subs.label: Observability
subs.desc: What does platform observability look like for a data system?

subs.label: Cost
subs.desc: How do you manage cost vs. SLA trade-offs in system design?

label: Distributed Systems Fundamentals
desc: 8 interview questions covering CAP Theorem, Consistency Models, Replication, Partitioning and more.

subs.label: CAP Theorem
subs.desc: What is the CAP theorem, and how does it shape data platform design?

subs.label: Consistency Models
subs.desc: Strong consistency guarantees every read sees the latest write, at the cost of latency and availability under partition — appropriate for something like a ledger balance or a feature store used for real-time decisions.

subs.label: Replication
subs.desc: Leader-follower (single-leader) replication routes all writes through one node and fans reads out to followers — simple to reason about, but the leader is a write bottleneck and failover involves promoting a follower.

subs.label: Partitioning
subs.desc: How do you partition or shard a large dataset, and what causes hot partitions?

subs.label: Consensus
subs.desc: At a high level, why do distributed systems need consensus algorithms like Paxos or Raft?

subs.label: Distributed Transactions
subs.desc: How do two-phase commit (2PC) and the Saga pattern differ for handling cross-system transactions?

subs.label: Event Ordering
subs.desc: Clocks on different machines drift and aren't perfectly synchronized even with NTP, so two events in true causal order can end up with out-of-order or identical timestamps once they cross machines.

subs.label: Quorum Systems
subs.desc: In an N-replica system, a quorum requires W (write) and R (read) nodes to acknowledge an operation such that W + R > N, guaranteeing overlap between any write set and any read set — that overlap is what lets a read see the latest write.

label: Storage & Database Selection
desc: 8 interview questions covering Database Selection, Storage Architecture, OLTP vs OLAP, Storage Formats and more.

subs.label: Database Selection
subs.desc: How do you decide between a SQL and a NoSQL database for a given system?

subs.label: Storage Architecture
subs.desc: A data warehouse is the right choice when consumers are BI/analytics workloads that need fast, structured, governed SQL access and you're willing to pay for schema-on-write and warehouse compute.

subs.label: OLTP vs OLAP
subs.desc: OLTP systems are optimized for many small, concurrent read/write transactions against a normalized schema — a single row insert/update, sub-millisecond latency, ACID guarantees.

subs.label: Storage Formats
subs.desc: Row-oriented storage keeps all columns of a record together on disk, which is efficient when you read or write whole records — the OLTP pattern.

subs.label: Indexing
subs.desc: Index the columns your queries actually filter, join, or sort on — every index speeds up reads but slows down writes and costs storage, so indexing everything "just in case" is a common anti-pattern.

subs.label: Caching
subs.desc: What are the main caching strategies, and how do you keep a cache consistent with its source of truth?

subs.label: Messaging Systems
subs.desc: How do you choose between Kafka, a cloud pub/sub service, and a traditional message queue for ingestion?

subs.label: Time-Series Design
subs.desc: How do you design storage for high-volume time-series or IoT sensor data?

label: Scalability & Capacity Planning
desc: 6 interview questions covering Scalability, Capacity Estimation, Hot Partitions, Backpressure and more.

subs.label: Scalability
subs.desc: Vertical scaling means adding more CPU/RAM/disk to a single node — simple, no distributed-systems complexity, but bounded by the biggest machine you can buy and creates a single point of failure.

subs.label: Capacity Estimation
subs.desc: How would you approach a back-of-the-envelope capacity estimation question in a system design interview?

subs.label: Hot Partitions
subs.desc: How do you detect and fix a hot key or hot partition once a system is already in production?

subs.label: Backpressure
subs.desc: Backpressure is what happens when a downstream consumer processes events slower than an upstream producer sends them — without handling it, the gap fills a buffer until it overflows and you either drop data or crash.

subs.label: Load Balancing
subs.desc: Round-robin is simplest and works well when requests are roughly uniform in cost, but breaks down if some requests are much more expensive than others.

subs.label: Auto-Scaling
subs.desc: How do you design auto-scaling for variable data pipeline load, like a batch cluster or a streaming consumer group?

label: Fault Tolerance, DR & High Availability
desc: 6 interview questions covering Disaster Recovery, Multi-Region Design, Failover Design, Backup Strategy and more.

subs.label: Disaster Recovery
subs.desc: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) is how much data you can afford to lose, measured in time — an RPO of 15 minutes means your backup/replication cadence must guarantee you never lose more than 15 minutes of data.

subs.label: Multi-Region Design
subs.desc: What's the difference between active-active and active-passive multi-region architecture, and what does each cost you?

subs.label: Failover Design
subs.desc: How do you design failover to avoid a split-brain scenario?

subs.label: Backup Strategy
subs.desc: What backup strategies would you use for a data platform, and how do you validate they actually work?

subs.label: Graceful Degradation
subs.desc: How do circuit breakers and graceful degradation apply to data pipeline design?

subs.label: Chaos Engineering
subs.desc: What is chaos engineering, and how would you apply it to a data pipeline?

label: Data Contracts, Governance & Security by Design
desc: 7 interview questions covering Access Control, PII & Masking, Data Lineage, Audit Logging and more.

subs.label: Access Control
subs.desc: Role-based access control (RBAC) grants permissions to roles rather than individuals, which scales better as headcount grows — you manage a handful of roles instead of per-person grants.

subs.label: PII & Masking
subs.desc: How do you design PII handling and data masking into a platform, rather than bolting it on afterward?

subs.label: Data Lineage
subs.desc: How would you design data lineage tracking into a platform?

subs.label: Audit Logging
subs.desc: How would you design audit logging for a data platform that needs to support a compliance investigation?

subs.label: Data Contracts
subs.desc: What is a data contract, and how do you design one between a producer and consumer team?

subs.label: Encryption Design
subs.desc: Encryption in transit (TLS between every service-to-service and client-to-service hop) protects data from network interception and is close to table-stakes today.

subs.label: Self-Serve Platform
subs.desc: How would you design a self-serve data platform that lets other teams build pipelines without your team as a bottleneck?

label: Applied System Design Case Studies
desc: 11 interview questions covering Case Study: Analytics Dashboard, Case Study: Log Aggregation, Case Study: Ride-Sharing, Case Study: Fraud Detection and more.

subs.label: Case Study: Analytics Dashboard
subs.desc: Events (page views, clicks) are produced from client SDKs into a durable log (Kafka/Kinesis), partitioned by a key like session or user ID so related events land on the same partition and preserve order.

subs.label: Case Study: Log Aggregation
subs.desc: Design a log aggregation and search platform, similar to the ELK stack or Splunk.

subs.label: Case Study: Ride-Sharing
subs.desc: Design the data pipeline for a ride-sharing platform (trip events, driver location, surge pricing).

subs.label: Case Study: Fraud Detection
subs.desc: Design a real-time fraud detection pipeline for financial transactions.

subs.label: Case Study: Recommendations
subs.desc: Design the offline/online data pipeline for a recommendation system.

subs.label: Case Study: Feature Store
subs.desc: Design a feature store for machine learning.

subs.label: Case Study: Notifications
subs.desc: Design a notification/alert delivery pipeline that needs to reach users across email, SMS, and push.

subs.label: Case Study: Metrics Platform
subs.desc: Design a metrics and monitoring platform, similar to Datadog or Prometheus, for ingesting time-series data at scale.

subs.label: Case Study: Data Catalog
subs.desc: Design a data catalog / metadata discovery platform for an organization with hundreds of datasets.

subs.label: Case Study: Payments Reconciliation
subs.desc: Design a reconciliation pipeline to catch discrepancies between a payments system and its downstream ledger.

subs.label: Case Study: GDPR Deletion
subs.desc: Design a data pipeline that can fulfill GDPR 'right to be forgotten' deletion requests across a data platform.

label: SLAs, Delivery & Cost at Scale
desc: 6 interview questions covering SLAs & Error Budgets, Freshness Monitoring, Cost Attribution, Deployment Strategy and more.

subs.label: SLAs & Error Budgets
subs.desc: An SLA is the external commitment, often with a consequence attached — "the daily sales table is available by 8am, 99.5% of the time." An SLO is the internal target you actually engineer to, usually stricter than the SLA to leave margin.

subs.label: Freshness Monitoring
subs.desc: How would you design end-to-end data freshness monitoring across a multi-stage pipeline?

subs.label: Cost Attribution
subs.desc: How do you design cost attribution or chargeback for a shared, multi-tenant data platform?

subs.label: Deployment Strategy
subs.desc: How would you design a safe deployment strategy (blue-green or canary) for changes to a production data pipeline?

subs.label: Testing Strategy
subs.desc: What testing strategy would you design for a data platform, beyond unit tests for transformation code?

subs.label: Internal Data APIs
subs.desc: How would you design an internal data API or service layer to serve derived data to other teams, instead of giving them direct table access?
